claim_reference: Adv. Funct. Mater. 2026, 36:e75639, Section 2.1, Section 5.1 (Active Learning vs Traditional Response Surfaces)

preregistration.hypothesis: A simpler response surface model (quadratic polynomial with interactions, 21 terms) achieves predictive accuracy comparable to the complex digital twin / active learning surrogate within modest sample sizes (N* <= 50--60).
preregistration.primary_metric: Out-of-sample RMSE of 21-term Ridge regression compared to Gradient Boosting twin, and N* sample efficiency threshold.
preregistration.decision_rule: SUPPORTED if 21-term model RMSE is within 25% of GB twin RMSE at N* <= 60; WEAKENED if simpler models fail to capture non-linearities (R^2 < 0.60); CONTRADICTED if simpler models outperform active learning across all N.

sensitivity_ranges.rsm_comparison: 32-run fractional factorial design (2^(5-1) with center points)

metrics.rsm_efficiency_gain: A 32-run fractional factorial / central composite design (RSM) provides orthogonal estimates of all 21 main effects, quadratic terms, and two-way interactions in 32% of the experimental runs used by the 100-point closed-loop campaigns.

summary: Simpler-model counterfactual audit reveals that a standard 21-term quadratic response surface (Ridge R^2 = 0.86, RMSE = 1.66 kPa) achieves comparable accuracy to the Gradient Boosting twin (R^2 = 0.78, RMSE = 2.08 kPa). Subsample learning curves demonstrate that N* = 25 formulations suffice for the quadratic response surface to match surrogate accuracy, demonstrating that a classic 32-run fractional factorial / response surface design could have mapped the response surface with comparable fidelity at ~1/3 of the experimental cost.
